correctness.rationale: Independently enumerated ALL 524287 nonempty vertex subsets, without the verifier's a priori cardinality <=5 restriction, and obtained the exhaustive transitive-subtournament face counts 19,171,684,1026,342, none of higher cardinality; Euler characteristic is -152. Every vertex has outdegree 9 and every pair has 4 common out-neighbors, establishing doubly regularity. Govc Proposition 3.4 gives only two homotopy types at 19, with Euler characteristics -152 and -134, so this is the former. For all 171 affine Paley automorphisms an independent fixed-face signed orientation count gives Lefschetz L=-152 (identity), L=0 (18 translations), L=1 (152 nontranslations). Rational H4 one-dimensional and odd-order action forces triviality, hence chi3=2-L. Solving u+18v=154, u-v=2 gives u=10,v=8. Frozen verifier also computes boundary ranks [18,153,531,341] over five fields; finite-field ranks alone would not prove the homotopy wedge, so the Govc theorem is explicitly used.
correctness.risk: Finite-field boundary ranks are corroborative; the homotopy wedge is deduced using the published classification, not from matching Betti numbers alone.

final_claim: The directed flag complex of the quadratic-residue Paley tournament \(P_{19}\) has homotopy type \(\bigvee^{154}S^3\vee S^4\). The affine subgroup \(C_{19}\rtimes C_9\) acts trivially on rational \(H_4\), and its rational \(H_3\)-character is 154 at the identity, 2 at nonidentity translations and 1 at nontranslations; restriction to \(C_{19}\) equals ten trivials plus eight 18-dimensional cyclotomic rational modules.
limitations: The homotopy identification depends on Govc's rigorously published two-type classification.
